chunks: And with the preceding chains of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, saying:

"Whoever acts according to what God has made obligatory upon him, he is among the best of people. And whoever avoids what God has forbidden him, he is among the most worshipful of people and the most pious of people. And whoever is content with what God has apportioned for him, he is among the richest of people."

key_terms.أورع: most pious — superlative of wara (scrupulous piety)
key_terms.افترض: made obligatory (fard) — refers to divinely mandated duties

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the best, most worshipful, and richest of people?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) presents a tripartite ethical framework: fulfilling divine obligations makes one the best of people, avoiding the forbidden makes one the most devout and pious, and contentment with God's provision makes one the richest. This teaching was conveyed through Abu Hamza al-Thumali, a close companion, and reflects the Imam's emphasis on practical spiritual refinement during a period when the Shia community looked to him for guidance after the tragedy of Karbala.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. And with the preceding chains of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Hamza who said: I heard ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, say:

"He who obediently acts according to what Allah has commanded him to do, he is the best of men on earth! And he who obediently refrains from that which Allah has forbidden him, he is the most worshipping servant, the most pious. And whoever is content with what Allah has apportioned to him, is the richest of all men."
